May 6, 1978
Dear Race Fan;
On behalf of Superamerica, Inc., the American Speed Assn. and Wisconsin
Auto Racing, Inc., welcome to the Superamerica 150 at the Wisconsin State
Fair Park Speedway.
The race is a new venture for the Milwaukee Mile. It brings together for
the first time here the real grass roots racers in a big track race event. It
also marks the first time in modern history that an early May event has
been scheduled and it welcomes a new major race sponsor.
Your reaction to the racing this weekend is extremely important. The size
and comments from the crowd may well determine the future of such racing
here, so I solicit your reaction to this weekend's racing.
If you are a regular fan here, you know this marks the begining of a ful
season of racing, which also includes a pair of Championship Trail events
and four for the stock cars, all sanctioned by the United States Auto Club.
If you are a newcomer and enjoy the events, why not join us for some of
the other races this season?
Sincerely,
John Kaishian, President
WISCONSIN AUTO RACING, INC.

Dick Trickle - A Look Back
Having started his stock car racing career at the age of 16,
Dick Trickle, of Wisconsin Rapids, now 36, is one of the most
experienced drivers in the Superamerica 150.
He cut his teeth on the short tracks of Central Wisconsin in
the late 1950s and early 1960s.
Trickle began to expand his horizons in 1968 and joined the

In 1972 Trickle set a national record by winning 67 features
at short tracks throughout the midwest.
With his extensive experience on the Milwaukee Mile
Trickle should be worth watching in the Superamerica 150.
